chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: The Clique Club in Philadelphia
summary: The Clique Club on Market Street had the longest bar and a turntable bandstand; Sears left and Ben Webster stayed until 1949.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: -- until after the Clique Club. We got to the Clique Club in Philadelphia. The Clique Club was a club on Market Street. It had the longest bar I've ever seen, a big long bar. There wasn't many tables but a bar forever. And, like, when you'd get ready to come on, you'd get on the bandstand and they'd turn you around on a table.
So whoever would -- when the band on the other side was finished, you know, he'd turn them around the back and you was out front.
I remember playing that with Cab Calloway.

And so then Ben stayed and Sears left; he left the band and he started to staying around New York. I think he got into song publishing, and a lot of things he did, Sears did. Ben stayed in the band. We kept that same band, and in 1949 Duke let him go.
